scope.purpose: Make the conventional reading values of the signs audible as an explicitly modern, synthetic and inspectable experiment.
must_not_be_labelled: reconstrucción de cómo hablaban los íberos

evidence_based_conventions.note: The five-vowel interpretation is broadly accepted; the exact ancient timbre remains unrecoverable.
Dental and velar dualities are voiced/voiceless in the profile. The historical contrast may instead have involved fortis/lenis features. The single labial series is rendered with a voiced onset.
These are conventional readable values, not measurements of ancient articulation.

explicit_hypotheses.note: The profile adopts a laminal versus apical/retracted contrast to make the two signs audibly distinct. Their historical phonetic values remain controversial.
Tap versus trill is retained only as IberoLab's audible project convention. The historical opposition between the two Iberian signs is unknown.
A syllabic nasal colour is used only so the token can be heard; scholarship also considers analyses involving a nasal plus a vocalic element.

non_historical_engineering_choices.timing: approximately equal duration per sign token
non_historical_engineering_choices.note: Pitch, formants, duration, rhythm, pauses and timbre are interface design parameters and carry no historical claim.

sources.citation: Moncunill Martí, Noemí; Velaza Frías, Javier (2020), Iberian, Palaeohispanica 20, 591-629.
Simkin, Oliver (2017), The Iberian sibilants revisited, Palaeohispanica 17, 207-233.
